rubric_notes: All must_include met: a.22.1.1/2/3/4 (+a.22.1.0) correctly named with sunids; superfamily = probable common ancestry; explicit refusal to transfer nucleosome function/DNA-binding/PTM sites to TAF/NC2/NF-Y/Sos/bacterial members. Correctly notes a.22 has a single superfamily so fold and superfamily coincide, and that fold alone would not imply homology. Correctly separates linker H1/H5 (a.4.5.13), HU/IHF (a.55.1), H-NS (a.155.1) as non-relatives. Domain-level lowest-shared-node claims are corroborated by the parents endpoints in the bundle. No material errors. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, superfamily, sunids, and superfamily curator comment (five active-site helices) all matching the bundle. Explains why superfamily is stronger than fold but weaker than family, rejects PR-ATP/histidine-pathway transfer to SSo12199 and MazG-role transfer to HisE, notes the hypothetical-protein and Li/UNL ligand caveats, and lists assays and alignments needed. Complete.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, sunids, and duplication comment, all supported by bundle. States superfamily co-membership as probable common origin with conserved duplicated core and nucleotide-binding motifs, and explicitly denies family-level transfer of substrate specificity, catalytic residue roles, regulation, oligomerization/polymerization, and ligand interactions; fold-level neighbours share only topology with no homology claim; template and automated-match caveats and need for independent evidence included. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Biological reasoning complete: superfamily as probable homology grounded in the bimetal-site comment, family split as sequence and chemistry divergence, fold-level similarity explicitly insufficient, function transfer refused with required metal-ligand and biochemical evidence named; appropriately hedges the evolutionary scenario as a curatorial hypothesis. Factual: misplaces rubrerythrin into the a.25.1.2 member list (SCOPe 2.08 places rubrerythrin N-terminal domain in a.25.1.1); loosely calls other a.25 superfamilies 'unrelated' before correctly stating SCOPe only withholds a homology claim. Other identifiers supported. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, superfamily, sunids, Pfam, protein-level members and curator comments. Clear remote-homology interpretation with 'probably related' hedge, refusal of copper/ET transfer, fold-level caveat, automated-match caveat and external-evidence requirements. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Families, sunids, example domains (d1ubia_, d1i42a_, d1c1yb_) and the Rap1A partner chain d1c1ya_ (c.37.1.8) all verified by bundle; lowest shared node d.15.1 correct. Superfamily correctly framed as probable common ancestry with structural (not functional) transfer. Explicitly rejects transfer of conjugation, ligand specificity (GTPase, p97, UBD), GO modifier terms, fold-level extension (MoaD/ThiS trap), and partner-chain confusion; within-RBD specificity caveat; automated-match provenance. Lists required family-level and experimental evidence. No material errors.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Families, sunids, Pfam mapping, fold comment, and KaiA annotation all bundle-supported. Correctly states homology rests on superfamily not fold, denies family-level closeness, rejects transfer of phosphorelay signaling, Mg2+ site, decarboxylase catalysis, and clock function, and treats the wing as a structural/oligomerization domain (recruitment). Description of the ODC major domain as a 'PLP-dependent transferase/beta-alpha barrel' is loose but hedged and non-release-specific.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Verified placement b.84.5/b.84.5.1, sunids, five sibling superfamilies with correct example members (cytochrome f small domain b.84.2.2, LytM b.84.3.2 confirmed in bundle), correct example domains and 'complexed with adp' annotation. Lowest shared node b.84 between d3a5ca3 and d1vf5c2 derivable from bundled parents. Evolutionary claim stated precisely: positive homology within b.84.5.1 (V1/A1 naming is not an evolutionary split), no ancestry asserted across superfamilies, and explicit that this is absence of evidence, not proof of independent origin. Rejects function/ligand transfer and sequence-alignment template use across superfamilies; lists external evidence needed. Complete.

Correct hierarchy, homology-endpoint interpretation, 'possible link' handled as suggestive but insufficient, convergence framed as possibility, external evidence listed. Unsupported release-history claim that f.21.1/f.21.2 'date from SCOP 1.63/1.65-era entries' is not backed by any retrieved evidence (hedged and plausible, so treated as unsupported rather than fabricated).

Family, superfamily, fold and class identifiers, sunids, fold comment, sole-superfamily status and family comments all match the bundle. Concise but complete: superfamily = probable common origin, different families = divergent sequence and function, fold-level similarity (including c.3/c.4 note) is weaker than superfamily and not proof of homology. Explicitly bars transfer of catalytic activity, NAD/NADP/CoA specificity, oligomeric state and physiological role, and names the independent evidence needed. Less detail than other answers but no omission of a required criterion. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage and identifiers (family k.40.1.1 sunid 100905, protein/species sunids, ligand comments), good class k reasoning and no-transfer limits. Omits the family node's 'not a true family' comment (not retrieved), relying solely on class k membership; decisive annotation ignored, bio ceiling <=2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 singleton fold vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 (verified in bundle); 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 and d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 under shared superfamily c.23.14 (verified); explicitly frames the move as a new superfamily-level common-ancestry assertion distinct from the tag-split boundary change. Correctly uses d1t1ja1 as current SID, notes class-only sharing in 1.69 carries no homology, cites 2.08 family comment (predicted activity, lacks last strand) with function-transfer and template caveats, honestly notes intermediate release not retrieved. No material errors.

Complete: correct artifact lineage for H:1-8, b.1.1.1 VH for H:9-111, clear statement that Artifacts class is bookkeeping and tag similarity is not homology evidence, practical exclusions, and the evidence types needed for real homology inference via d1a14h1. All facts supported by bundle.

Correct 1.75 whole-chain record and correct 2.08 pair with sunids, boundaries, and the class change, plus a clear three-part account of what changed. Good module reasoning from the populated PA14-like superfamily against the singleton C-terminal superfamily, with level-calibrated transfer limits and template cautions. Does not name 2.04 as the release introducing the split, and asserts a specific cluster representative and percent identity for this chain without supporting retrieved evidence.

Correct five-domain decomposition, correct lineages and boundaries, mosaic/group II intron interpretation with appropriate superfamily-vs-fold caveats and no function transfer; new fold d.394 for d3jb9a5 A:47-697 correctly identified. One noncentral imprecision: describes the d.394 lineage as a '2.08-era addition' when it was introduced in 2.07 (not verified in its bundle).

Dense but complete: shared family a.298.1.1 with lineage and protein-node sunids, lengths 51/373/752, the canonical repeat unit defined on 4cj9 A:259-292 and propagated to members, the 're' flag with its definition, and the 'single repeat' comment on d2kq5a_. Explains the single-domain treatment of the solenoid, states that fold-level similarity alone would not establish homology, and rejects naive function transfer given differing repeat counts and the Burkholderia member. Reading 'complexed with se' as a selenium note is a defensible interpretation. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct 2.08 / 2.08-stable / 2.08-2026-08-16 reporting matches evidence. Cites 2.08-stable pinned to release=2.08 rather than the unpinned 'current' alias; preserves both stable and periodic date when post-freeze entries are used. Periodic semantics correct (automated additions on top of frozen tree without altering it). Useful is_comprehensive caveat.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All must_include met: same family a.47.2.1 for fragments and full domain; fold label retained by family-level sequence identity, not fragment shape; explicit statement that fragment-based fold assignments are provisional until confirmed by a full-length structure, which here confirmed the fold. Correctly cites 'ms' heterogeneity flag, spectrin resemblance as a.7 fold-level only, six a.47 superfamilies not homologous, 1dn1 obsolete/automated match to d3c98b_, function-transfer caveat and representative choice. All identifiers, sunids and lengths match the bundle; no material errors.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Makes the requested inference: divergence within c.2.1, fold-level grouping is topological only, c.2/c.3/c.4 treated as unresolved rather than proven convergent; lists integrated evidence (core topology, conserved motifs in equivalent positions, profile/HMM, whole-core structural alignment) and transfer limits. Factual slip: lists the FwdE/GAPDH domain-like fold d.81 as a location of NAD-binding domains, whereas d.81.1 is the GAPDH catalytic domain. Other sunids, family lists and curator comments match the bundle.

Compact but correct on the core change: 2.04 b.23.2.1 under the CUB-like fold versus b.18.1.3, lowest shared node the all-beta class, and current shared superfamily b.18.1 with distinct families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3. Cites the curated PubMed 17977833 note, the jelly-roll lectin-like topology, and the shared non-catalytic binding-module role, and bars specific function transfer and template use. Loses credit for thin development of the evidence types, no statement that a 2.04 different-fold placement is not a positive analogy claim, an unretrieved deterministic comparison result, and an unsupported assertion about what curators judged regarding core strand arrangement.

Sequences from bundle used to show point-mutant relationship; hf definition quoted; homology retained at protein/species level; explains why high sequence identity is a trap for coordinate transfer; training label mismatch, function transfer limits (NHE heterogen, not DNA), representative selection, and filtering or separate labeling of hf domains. States SCOPe does not quantify deviation and names external superposition/literature needed.

Lineage, fr flag, 50-of-99 observed vs 104-of-104, 1uc6 quality match bundle; 1o5d quality correct. States homology at family level unaffected, alignment covers at most ~50 residues so weak scores are not divergence, coverage relative to full length, fragment not a template, fragments excluded/down-weighted from representative sets, quality scores do not override fr flag, d1uc6a1 better of the two with comparison among complete domains, fragment not independent evidence of variation, no function transfer, flag is domain-scope and non-inherited. Noncentral factual error: describes 1o5d as a uPA complex (partner domains indicate factor VIIa); suggests d1o5dt1 as a tissue-factor reference without noting it is domain 1 not domain 2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Concise but complete: new superfamily in existing fold; family = shared ancestor claim; superfamily split = shared topology only, hedged as convergence/constraint/undetectable ancestry; new fold = distinct core topology and explicitly 'not the way to express not homologous'. States fold similarity or FATCAT hit alone does not establish homology, lists positive homology evidence required, frames assignment as revisable evolutionary hypothesis, rejects function transfer. c.1 (sunid 51350) with 34 superfamilies supported by children bundle (has_more=false). No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

All three families, superfamily, fold and sibling families correctly identified with bundle-supported sunids; ATP-grasp/PIPK curator comment correctly treated as similarity note, not homology. Gives superfamily-level common ancestry and shared catalytic core/mechanism, then clearly limits substrate class and regulation to family/protein level with named unsafe transfers (activation-loop phosphorylation, p85, cyclins). Evidence requirements complete (family-level sequence, specificity-determinant alignment, substrate-bound structures, kinetics/phosphosite mapping, regulation assays, genomic context). No material errors.
